notes: The first archive backfill: one month of San Francisco YIMBY's paged archive, 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31, listed by `poll.py backfill` and screened by the same screen the daily poll uses. Every queued story was read in full.

coverage.remaining: The 39 items the screen skipped in this window, each with its recorded reason, and every San Francisco YIMBY month before 2026-07 and between 2026-08-01 and the daily poll's reach. The other seven routed feeds are untouched for July 2026: mission-local, the-registry, sf-standard, sf-examiner, sf-chronicle, sf-examiner-social and the-voice-sf, together 2,498 stories listed and 517 queued.
coverage.note: Sixty stories were listed for the window and 21 queued, a far higher rate than the register's general newsrooms — this outlet writes about nothing but buildings and tags each item with its street address. Every article carries a related-articles rail naming 10 South Van Ness Avenue, 536 Mission Street and 2500 Mariposa Street at 90 per cent or more into the page; those are furniture, not reporting, and none was extracted.

findings.description: An application has been filed to convert part of the ground-level garage at 3571 16th Street in the Castro into three accessory dwelling units, replacing eight covered parking spaces under a local ordinance. Each new unit would have two bedrooms and two bathrooms, and two of the three would open onto the shared backyard; the twelve existing apartments are untouched. Syncopated Architecture drew the plans and Structure Properties is the owner. The article describes the existing 33-foot structure as recorded built in 1963 by an unknown architect in the Midcentury Modern style, and puts construction cost at about two-thirds of a million dollars, excluding other development costs. The conversion is proposed, not built, so nothing goes into the building block.

Schaub Li Architects is responsible for the design and AHK Group is the owner, filing through One Timberlake Inc. findings.description: The affordable housing at 2550 Irving Street, a block from Golden Gate Park, has filled every one of its 90 units, completing occupancy of a building that topped out in the winter of 2025-26. The 78-foot structure holds more than 113,000 square feet: nine studios, 34 one-bedroom, 23 two-bedroom and 24 three-bedroom apartments, let to households earning 30 to 80 per cent of area median income, with 22 homes subsidised for families leaving homelessness and 15 for formerly homeless veterans. Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corporation developed it and PYATOK designed it: a podium complex broken into three masses, clad in sandstone-toned thin brick, precast concrete, fibre cement, painted aluminium and western red cedar. It is all-electric, on a pilot model for the International Living Future Institute, with an 18-car garage stacker and storage for 90 bicycles.

findings.description: Updated plans have been filed for the redevelopment of the Safeway at 15 Marina Boulevard, raising the residential capacity from 790 to 848 apartments while slightly reducing the floor count. The 258-foot scheme would yield about 989,500 square feet: 746,600 of housing, 33,840 of amenities, 67,180 for a new Safeway and 141,960 for a 349-car garage, with 360 bicycle spaces and a mix of 254 studios, 268 one-bedroom, 212 two-bedroom and 114 three-bedroom homes, 86 of them deed-restricted at about half of area median income. Arquitectonica designed two towers of 18 and 22 floors on a shared podium. Align Real Estate is the sponsor, filing for the owner, Albertsons Companies. Preliminary permits were filed in December 2025 and the city found the application eligible for streamlining under AB 2011 in March 2026; the revised filing resets the review clock.

findings.description: Formal permits have been filed to replace the vacant Empire Theater at 85 West Portal Avenue with a nine-storey building of 64 apartments over ground-floor retail. The 112-foot scheme would yield about 113,670 square feet — 94,400 of housing in 16 one-bedroom, 36 two-bedroom and 12 three-bedroom homes, 13,300 of parking for 27 cars and 64 bicycles, and 4,100 of retail — with ten homes deed-restricted below market rate, five at 50 and five at 120 per cent of area median income, invoking AB 1287 and the State Density Bonus law for a 100 per cent density bonus, and AB 2011 and SB 330 to streamline review. Handel Architects designed it in terracotta and off-white concrete panels, reading as two buildings over West Portal Avenue and Vicente Street, and keeping the theatre's ornamental cornice above the new retail while the rest of the century-old building is demolished. DM Development is filing for the owner, Empire West Portal LLC. The article records the cinema as running from 1925 to 2021, opening as the Portal Theater and renamed the Empire Theater in 1936. Construction is estimated at about $45 million, with completion as early as 2028.

findings.description: The affordable housing at 78 Haight Street in Hayes Valley opened in July 2026, adding 64 homes to a parcel on the former Central Freeway corridor that was cleared after the Loma Prieta earthquake. Half the apartments are for transitional-age youth leaving homelessness and half for low-income families, with support services provided in partnership with Larkin Street Youth Services. Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corporation developed it; Guzman Construction Group and Suffolk built it in a joint venture, with Guzman as general contractor. Paulett Taggart Architects designed the seven-storey building — white fibre cement with sawtooth bay windows over Octavia Street — and TS Studio was the landscape architect. It cost about $54 million, of which $21 million came from the Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development and $4 million from California's No Place Like Home programme, with further funding from Silicon Valley Bank and Merritt Community Capital.

findings.description: The Planning Department has granted final approval for a 23-storey tower at 1965 Market Street, at the corner of Duboce Avenue, entitling 201 apartments in under two years. The 239-foot building would yield about 237,650 square feet — 206,060 of housing, 2,450 of retail and 16,500 for an underground garage — in ten studios, 100 one-bedroom, 81 two-bedroom and ten three-bedroom homes, 30 of them deed-restricted below market rate across low and moderate incomes, with parking for 62 cars and 138 bicycles. SB 330, SB 423 and the State Density Bonus law raised capacity nearly 89 per cent above base zoning, with waivers for rear yard, open space, dwelling-unit exposure, ground-floor commercial use, parking sizes and retail concessions. Keller Grover Properties is the developer and RG Architecture the designer; the tower now reads as a single mass rising from the existing Spanish Revival podium, clad in precast glass-fibre-reinforced concrete and painted steel. The article states the three-storey structure on the site was built in 1926 and held a mortuary and two apartments.

findings.description: New building permits have been filed for a five-storey apartment infill at 4148 24th Street in Noe Valley, between Castro and Diamond streets, following the city's final approval of the project in July 2025. The 52-foot building would hold about 9,700 square feet of housing across four full floors and a mezzanine: seven two-bedroom apartments, one deed-restricted affordable, with a bike room and a ground-floor flat opening onto a private garden. RKD Consulting drew the plans — smooth fibre cement, stucco and concrete, balconies over 24th Street, pixelated stucco side panels. Golden Properties LLC is the owner. Demolition permits for the existing three-storey Mission Revival building, which has a ground-floor shop and a vacant flat, have not yet been filed. Construction is estimated at about $2.5 million.
